1: From prison, near death, Paul writes to Timothy and recalls the faith of his grandmother Lois and mother Eunice. He tells him to fan into flame the gift he received through the laying on of hands, and not to be ashamed of the Gospel.
Faith is often handed down in families. God gives a spirit of power, love and self-control, not of fear.
2: Timothy is to entrust the teaching to faithful people who can teach others. Like a soldier, an athlete and a farmer, he must endure hardship. He should avoid pointless quarrels and correct opponents gently.
This chain of teachers handing on the faith is apostolic tradition in action. "If we are faithless, he remains faithful."
3: In the last days people will love themselves, money and pleasure more than God. Timothy should continue in what he learned from childhood. All Scripture is inspired by God and useful for teaching, correcting and training in righteousness.
Scripture is God-breathed. It equips us for every good work.
4: Paul charges Timothy to preach the word whether it is welcome or not. He knows his death is near: he has finished the race and kept the faith. Almost everyone has left him, but the Lord stood by him.
These are among Paul's last words. He faces death with confidence in the Lord, the just judge.
